Q: Are Azure AI Search Indexers useful for real-time embedding? A:

Azure AI Search Indexer can be scheduled as discussed above. For real-time trigger, you will have to use either an Azure Function App or Azure Logic App and watch for a file-upload event via BLOB storage trigger.

You should also enable Soft Delete on your BLOB container for removing vector indexes for stale/deleted docs from BLOB storage. As new versions get uploaded, you should remove older versions from your vector indexes. An automatic way of doing this is to Enable Soft Delete policy on your BLOB container. Azure AI Search will automatically delete older versions of documents and keep your vector index relevant.

Q: Why doesn't this regex with "\d" work for grep? A:

By default, grep uses basic regular expression and \d is (PCRE) syntax. It is not supported so you'll need to use ( [0-9] ) or ( [[:digit:]] ) instead, or use grep with option -P

Why doesn't [0-9]+ work?

  • In BRE, meta-characters like + lose their meaning and need to be escaped.

You can fix this by using one of the following:

grep -v "Packet number [0-9]\+ doesn't match"

OR

grep -v "Packet number [[:digit:]]\+ doesn't match"

Q: JPA Many To Many relationship add method A:

The helper method ensures that both sides of the bi-directional relation are updated. The scope has the location and the location has the scope and that is true immediately in memory, just as if you hade saved and then loaded everything in a new session. Doing that in the helper method ensures that it is always done as long as the helper method is used everywhere. Furthermore some classes return immutable sets (wrapping the original versions) from the public get methods and then you have no choice. If you want to add you must use the add method. I like that.

Updating the other side manually also works. Partly it is a matter of style and preference. However, I would recommend picking a convention and following it for a given project.

Q: Plotly Express facets show no lines when setting x-axis range and custom tick labels A:

It seems it doesn't calculate range in yaxis when you manually set range in xaxis

It may need to:

  • manually add range in yaxis

    fig.update_yaxes(range=[df["rssi_mean"].min(), df["rssi_mean"].max()])

  • force it do calculate range

    fig.update_yaxes(autorange=True)

fig.update_xaxes(
    range=[start, end],  # always 08:00–20:00
    tickmode="array",
    tickvals=tickvals,
    ticktext=ticktext,
)

#fig.update_yaxes(range=[df["rssi_mean"].min(), df["rssi_mean"].max()])  # set range manually
fig.update_yaxes(autorange=True)  # force it to calculat range

fig.show()
